subject.title: feat: raise (or remove) 3-minute no-output watchdog cap on CLI requests

question: Should ordinary inherited resumed CLI-backed user runs keep the 180-second no-output guard, move to a longer bounded default, or gain explicit disable/tuning semantics?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves the inherited resume guard after the configured-timeout fix, while raising or disabling it changes availability, stuck-process recovery, and config compatibility tradeoffs for existing users.

options.title: Approve a bounded longer default
options.body: Raise the inherited resume ceiling through the existing watchdog defaults, keep the watchdog enabled, and require focused resolver/runtime proof plus upgrade notes.

options.title: Add explicit tuning or disable semantics
options.body: Accept a `0` or `null` style no-cap mode only with schema, docs, compatibility tests, and an explicit maintainer decision on public config semantics.

options.title: Keep the 180-second inherited guard
options.body: Leave current behavior intact and document per-backend watchdog overrides for operators with known long silent CLI workloads.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded longer default
recommendation.body: Raise the inherited resume ceiling through the existing watchdog defaults, keep the watchdog enabled, and require focused resolver/runtime proof plus upgrade notes.
